title: Leviticus Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Leviticus chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Leviticus Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Leviticus Chapter 6.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 6:2, what kind of sin involves lying to one's neighbor about something delivered to keep or taken by violence?
options: Trespass against the LORD
Idolatry
Blasphemy
Theft only
questions.correctAnswer: Trespass against the LORD
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:2 states that if a soul sin and commit a trespass against the LORD by lying to his neighbor about something delivered to keep or taken by violence, it is a sin.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 6:3 mentions that swearing falsely about found lost property is considered sinning.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:3 describes that if a man finds what is lost and lies about it or swears falsely, he is sinning.

questions.question: What must a person do if he has sinned by deceitfully getting or taking away something, according to Leviticus 6:4?
options: Give a tenth of it to the poor
Restore what was taken or gotten deceitfully
Offer a burnt offering only
Make a public confession
questions.correctAnswer: Restore what was taken or gotten deceitfully
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:4 commands that if a person has sinned, he must restore what he took violently away or deceitfully gotten.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 6:5, how much extra must be added when restoring what was taken or sworn about falsely?
options: One tenth more
One half more
The fifth part more
Double the amount
questions.correctAnswer: The fifth part more
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:5 states that he shall restore the principal plus the fifth part more to the one to whom it belongs.

questions.question: What kind of animal is to be brought as a trespass offering according to Leviticus 6:6?
options: A ram without blemish
A young goat
A bullock
A dove
questions.correctAnswer: A ram without blemish
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:6 instructs that the trespass offering shall be a ram without blemish from the flock.

questions.question: True or False: The priest shall make atonement for the sinner and the trespass shall be forgiven, as stated in Leviticus 6:7.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:7 affirms that the priest shall make atonement for the sinner before the LORD and he shall be forgiven.

questions.question: What is the main reason the burnt offering fire must burn all night to the morning, according to Leviticus 6:9?
options: To keep the altar warm
Because of the burning upon the altar all night
To prevent animals from approaching
To signify the end of the day
questions.correctAnswer: Because of the burning upon the altar all night
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:9 says the burnt offering is because of the burning upon the altar all night unto the morning.

questions.question: What garments does the priest put on when taking up the ashes from the altar, as described in Leviticus 6:10?
options: Linen garment and linen breeches
Woolen robe and sandals
Golden vestments
No special clothing
questions.correctAnswer: Linen garment and linen breeches
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:10 states the priest shall put on his linen garment and linen breeches when taking up the ashes.

questions.question: True or False: According to Leviticus 6:11, the priest carries the ashes without the camp to a clean place after putting on other garments.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:11 says the priest shall put off his garments, put on others, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 6:12, what must not be put out on the altar fire?
options: The priest's linen garments
The fire upon the altar
The incense burner
The lamps
questions.correctAnswer: The fire upon the altar
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:12 commands that the fire upon the altar shall be burning and shall not be put out.

questions.question: Which of the following is part of the law of the meat offering as described in Leviticus 6:14?
options: The sons of Aaron shall offer it before the LORD
The people shall eat all of it
It must be offered only on the Sabbath
It should be burned entirely
questions.correctAnswer: The sons of Aaron shall offer it before the LORD
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:14 states that the sons of Aaron shall offer the meat offering before the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 6:15 commands that a handful of the meat offering, along with oil and frankincense, shall be burned on the altar for a sweet savour unto the LORD.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:15 instructs the priest to take a handful of the flour, oil, and frankincense from the meat offering and burn it on the altar as a memorial.

questions.question: In Leviticus 6, which comes first: the instruction to restore what was taken by violence or the command for the priest to burn the fire upon the altar continually?
options: Restore what was taken by violence
Burn the fire upon the altar continually
Put on linen garments
Offer the sin offering
questions.correctAnswer: Restore what was taken by violence
questions.explanation: The instruction to restore what was taken violently appears in Leviticus 6:4 before the command to keep the fire burning continually in Leviticus 6:13.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 6:16, where shall Aaron and his sons eat the remainder of the meat offering?
options: In the holy place within the court of the tabernacle
In the city marketplace
In the wilderness outside the camp
At their own homes
questions.correctAnswer: In the holy place within the court of the tabernacle
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:16 states that Aaron and his sons shall eat the remainder with unleavened bread in the holy place, in the court of the tabernacle.

questions.question: What kind of bread must be used with the meat offering according to Leviticus 6:17?
options: Unleavened bread
Leavened bread
Barley bread
Honey cake
questions.correctAnswer: Unleavened bread
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:17 specifies that the meat offering shall not be baked with leaven but with unleavened bread.

medium.title: Leviticus Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Leviticus Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What must the priest do with the ashes from the burnt offering according to Leviticus 6:11?
options: Put them beside the altar
Carry them forth without the camp to a clean place
Scatter them on the ground near the altar
Burn them completely on the altar
questions.correctAnswer: Carry them forth without the camp to a clean place
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:11 instructs the priest to put off his garments, put on other garments, and carry the ashes without the camp to a clean place. This shows the care taken to keep the camp ceremonially clean by removing ashes.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 6:12, what is the priest commanded to do every morning regarding the altar fire?
options: Put out the fire and rekindle it at night
Add wood to keep the fire burning
Clean the ashes off the altar
Offer a sin offering
questions.correctAnswer: Add wood to keep the fire burning
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:12 states the priest shall burn wood on the altar every morning to keep the fire burning, and lay the burnt offering in order upon it, emphasizing continual devotion and worship.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 6:13 say about the fire upon the altar?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:13 clearly states that the fire shall ever be burning upon the altar and shall never go out, symbolizing perpetual worship and God's continual presence.

questions.question: Who is commanded to offer the meat offering before the LORD as described in Leviticus 6:14?
options: The sons of Aaron
The elders of Israel
The Levites
All the people of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The sons of Aaron
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:14 instructs that the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall offer the meat offering before the LORD, showing the special priestly role in worship.

questions.question: What is to be done with the handful taken from the meat offering according to Leviticus 6:15?
options: It shall be eaten by the priests
It shall be burned upon the altar for a sweet savour
It shall be given to the poor
It shall be stored for the next offering
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be burned upon the altar for a sweet savour
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:15 teaches that the priest shall take a handful of the flour, oil, and frankincense from the meat offering and burn it on the altar as a memorial sweet savour unto the LORD, symbolizing dedication and remembrance.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 6:16, where and how shall Aaron and his sons eat the remainder of the meat offering?
options: Anywhere in Israel with leavened bread
In the holy place with unleavened bread
In their homes with unleavened bread
Only outside the camp with leavened bread
questions.correctAnswer: In the holy place with unleavened bread
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:16 specifies that Aaron and his sons shall eat the remainder of the meat offering in the holy place, in the court of the tabernacle, and it must be eaten with unleavened bread, emphasizing holiness and purity.

questions.question: What restriction is given about baking the meat offering in Leviticus 6:17?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:17 states the meat offering shall not be baked with leaven, indicating that it must be unleavened, which represents purity and separation from sin.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 6:18 describe the holiness required of those who eat the offerings made by fire?
options: Only priests may eat, but no holiness is required
All males among Aaron’s children shall eat, and everyone who touches the offerings shall be holy
Only the high priest may eat, and the offerings are common
Anyone may eat if they declare themselves holy
questions.correctAnswer: All males among Aaron’s children shall eat, and everyone who touches the offerings shall be holy
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:18 emphasizes that all males among Aaron's children shall eat the offerings, and it is a statute forever that everyone who touches them must be holy, highlighting the sacredness of the offerings and those who partake.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 6:20 say about the portion and timing of the meat offering for Aaron and his sons?
options: They shall offer a tenth of an ephah of fine flour once a day at noon
They shall offer a tenth of an ephah of fine flour, half in the morning and half at night
They shall offer a tenth of an ephah of fine flour only at night
They shall offer a tenth of an ephah of fine flour only in the morning
questions.correctAnswer: They shall offer a tenth of an ephah of fine flour, half in the morning and half at night
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:20 instructs that on the day Aaron is anointed, he and his sons shall offer a perpetual meat offering of a tenth part of an ephah of fine flour, half in the morning and half at night, reflecting continual dedication.

questions.question: Based on Leviticus 6:11-13, what biblical virtue is taught through the continual burning of the altar fire?
options: Faithfulness and perseverance in worship
Generosity towards neighbors
Humility in service
Forgiveness of sins
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness and perseverance in worship
questions.explanation: Verses 11-13 describe the altar fire as never to be put out, symbolizing ongoing worship and faithfulness. This teaches perseverance and continual devotion to God.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 6:15-16 teach about the importance of integrity and holiness in offerings?
options: By allowing anyone to eat the offering anywhere
By requiring the offering to be burned completely without remainder
By commanding a portion to be burned as a memorial and the remainder eaten by priests in a holy place with unleavened bread
By permitting the offering to be mixed with leaven
questions.correctAnswer: By commanding a portion to be burned as a memorial and the remainder eaten by priests in a holy place with unleavened bread
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:15-16 shows that part of the offering is burned for God’s remembrance and the rest eaten only by priests in a holy place with unleavened bread, illustrating reverence, integrity, and holiness in worship.

questions.question: A fellow believer struggles with following daily spiritual disciplines. Based on Leviticus 6:12-13, what biblical truth about spiritual consistency can encourage them?
options: Spiritual fire can be extinguished and rekindled at will
God requires continual, faithful devotion symbolized by the never-ending altar fire
Only occasional worship is necessary
Spiritual effort is unnecessary if one prays occasionally
questions.correctAnswer: God requires continual, faithful devotion symbolized by the never-ending altar fire
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:12-13 teaches that the altar fire must never go out and wood must be added every morning, symbolizing the need for consistent, faithful worship and spiritual discipline.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 6:17-18, what is the consequence for anyone who touches the offerings of the LORD made by fire?
options: They must offer a burnt offering
They shall be considered unclean forever
They shall be holy
They must fast for seven days
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be holy
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:18 states that every one who touches the offerings made by fire shall be holy, emphasizing the call to holiness in those who handle sacred things.

questions.question: The meat offering of Aaron and his sons is described as perpetual in Leviticus 6:20-22. What does this teach about their role in spiritual leadership?
options: Their service is temporary and optional
Their role requires continuous dedication and intercession
They serve only during festivals
They may delegate their duties freely
questions.correctAnswer: Their role requires continuous dedication and intercession
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:20-22 describes a perpetual meat offering, meaning Aaron and his sons’ priestly duties were ongoing, teaching that spiritual leadership demands continual dedication and intercession for the people.

questions.question: True or False: According to Leviticus 6:23, every meat offering for the priest shall be wholly burnt and not eaten.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:23 specifies that every meat offering for the priest shall be wholly burnt and shall not be eaten, but this refers specifically to certain offerings. Other offerings, like the meat offering, may be eaten by priests as per earlier verses (6:16-18).

hard.title: Leviticus Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Leviticus Chapter 6.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 6, what must be done with the meat offering for the priest?
options: It shall be wholly burnt and not eaten
It shall be eaten only by the high priest
It shall be given to the poor
It shall be shared with the congregation
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be wholly burnt and not eaten
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:23 states that every meat offering for the priest shall be wholly burnt and shall not be eaten, emphasizing the sacredness and total dedication of this offering to the LORD.

questions.question: Who is authorized to offer the meat offering when Aaron is replaced?
options: The priest of his sons that is anointed in his stead
Moses himself
Any Levite
The oldest son of Aaron
questions.correctAnswer: The priest of his sons that is anointed in his stead
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:22 specifies that the priest of Aaron's sons who is anointed in his place shall offer the meat offering, showing the continuity of the priestly function through anointed successors.

questions.question: What is the significance of the fire upon the altar as described in Leviticus 6?
options: It shall never go out and burn continually
It shall be extinguished every Sabbath
It is symbolic of the sun god
It is only lit during festivals
questions.correctAnswer: It shall never go out and burn continually
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:13 commands that the fire upon the altar shall ever be burning and never go out, symbolizing God's continual presence and acceptance of offerings.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 6:25-30, where must the sin offering be killed?
options: In the place where the burnt offering is killed
Outside the camp
At the entrance of the tabernacle
In the holy of holies
questions.correctAnswer: In the place where the burnt offering is killed
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:25 states that the sin offering shall be killed in the same place as the burnt offering, marking a specific sacred location for these sacrificial acts.

questions.question: How are the priests to treat the blood of the sin offering when it is sprinkled on garments?
options: They must wash the garments in the holy place
They must burn the garments
They must leave the garments as they are
They must bury the garments outside the camp
questions.correctAnswer: They must wash the garments in the holy place
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:27 commands that if blood of the sin offering is sprinkled on garments, they should be washed in the holy place, underscoring ritual purity requirements.

questions.question: What is the requirement for the vessels used to boil the sin offering meat, according to Leviticus 6?
options: Earthen vessels must be broken; brass pots must be scoured and rinsed
All vessels must be made of gold
Wooden vessels are preferred
No vessels are allowed
questions.correctAnswer: Earthen vessels must be broken; brass pots must be scoured and rinsed
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:28 instructs that earthen vessels used for boiling must be broken, and brass pots must be thoroughly cleaned, reflecting the sanctity and the need for cleansing in the ritual process.

questions.question: What does the term 'most holy' refer to in the context of the sin offering and trespass offering in Leviticus 6?
options: They are set apart exclusively for the priests
They are offerings for the whole congregation
They are offerings for the poor
They are offerings for the Levites only
questions.correctAnswer: They are set apart exclusively for the priests
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:17 and 6:29 describe these offerings as 'most holy,' meaning they are especially sanctified and reserved for the priests’ consumption, indicating their elevated status in the sacrificial system.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word 'trespass offering' as used in Leviticus 6, and what does it imply about the nature of the sin?
options: Chatat, meaning sin or guilt offering, implying unintentional sins
Olah, meaning burnt offering, implying voluntary devotion
Minchah, meaning gift offering, implying gratitude
Shelem, meaning peace offering, implying fellowship
questions.correctAnswer: Chatat, meaning sin or guilt offering, implying unintentional sins
questions.explanation: The term 'trespass offering' corresponds to the Hebrew 'Chatat,' which refers to sin or guilt offerings primarily for unintentional sins or offenses, as detailed in Leviticus 6:1-7 and cross-referenced in Leviticus 5:14-19.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the fulfillment of the sin offering concept described in Leviticus 6 through Jesus Christ?
options: Hebrews 9:22-28
Matthew 5:17-20
Romans 12:1-2
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews 9:22-28
questions.explanation: Hebrews 9:22-28 references the necessity of blood for the remission of sins, fulfilling the typology of sin offerings described in Leviticus 6, showing how Christ's sacrifice supersedes the old covenant offerings.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Leviticus 6:13 regarding the altar fire, and what does it symbolize?
options: Inclusio, symbolizing God's perpetual presence
Metaphor, symbolizing the sun
Simile, comparing the fire to a lion
Allegory, representing Israel’s history
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio, symbolizing God's perpetual presence
questions.explanation: The phrase 'The fire shall ever be burning... it shall never go out' in Leviticus 6:13 employs inclusio, framing the sacrificial instructions with a symbol of God's constant presence and acceptance of offerings.

questions.question: What is the specific instruction for the consumption of the meat offering leftovers in Leviticus 6?
options: Aaron and his sons shall eat it with unleavened bread in the holy place
It shall be shared with the entire congregation
It must be burned completely
It should be given to the poor outside the camp
questions.correctAnswer: Aaron and his sons shall eat it with unleavened bread in the holy place
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:16 explains that the remainder of the meat offering, after the designated portion is burned, shall be eaten by Aaron and his sons with unleavened bread in the holy place, showing the sacred privilege and ritual purity required.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 6:5 prescribe restitution for one who has sworn falsely about something delivered to keep or taken away by violence?
options: Restore the principal plus a fifth part more and give it to the owner
Offer a burnt offering only
Pay double the value to the priest
Confess and fast for three days
questions.correctAnswer: Restore the principal plus a fifth part more and give it to the owner
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:5 requires that the offender restore what was taken or sworn falsely about, plus an additional one-fifth, to the rightful owner, emphasizing restitution in the process of atonement.

questions.question: True or False: According to Leviticus 6:26, the priest who offers the sin offering must eat it in the holy place.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:26 states that the priest who offers the sin offering shall eat it in the holy place, underscoring the sanctity of those who partake in the offerings.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 6 commands that the fire on the altar may be extinguished each evening and rekindled every morning.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:12-13 clearly commands that the fire on the altar shall burn continually and never go out, symbolizing God’s perpetual presence and acceptance of offerings.

questions.question: Which earlier Old Testament book contains laws that are most closely related to the trespass offering laws found in Leviticus 6?
options: Numbers
Exodus
Deuteronomy
Genesis
questions.correctAnswer: Numbers
questions.explanation: Numbers 5:5-10 contains laws concerning restitution and trespass offerings, closely paralleling the laws in Leviticus 6, highlighting the development of Israel’s sacrificial system.

theological.title: Leviticus Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Leviticus Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 6:4, what must a person do if they have sinned by deceitfully obtaining or taking away something?
options: Restore what was taken or deceitfully gotten
Offer a burnt offering only
Confess publicly before the congregation
Fast for seven days
questions.correctAnswer: Restore what was taken or deceitfully gotten
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:4 instructs that the sinner must restore what was taken violently, deceitfully gotten, or lost and found, showing the requirement of restitution as part of repentance.

questions.question: What additional requirement is placed on restitution besides restoring the principal amount according to Leviticus 6:5?
options: Add one-fifth more to the principal
Add double the amount as a penalty
Offer a sin offering without restitution
Give a freewill offering instead
questions.correctAnswer: Add one-fifth more to the principal
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:5 requires the sinner to restore the principal plus a fifth part more, emphasizing God's justice and mercy in the restitution process.

questions.question: What is the nature of the trespass offering described in Leviticus 6:6?
options: A ram without blemish from the flock
A young bull without defect
A lamb with a broken wing
Two turtledoves or pigeons
questions.correctAnswer: A ram without blemish from the flock
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:6 specifies the trespass offering as a ram without blemish, signifying the necessity of a perfect sacrifice for atonement.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 6:7 teach about the role of the priest in relation to the trespass offering?
options: The priest makes atonement and grants forgiveness
The priest only burns the offering without atonement
The priest confesses on behalf of the sinner
The priest offers a meal to the congregation
questions.correctAnswer: The priest makes atonement and grants forgiveness
questions.explanation: According to Leviticus 6:7, the priest's role is to make atonement before the LORD, resulting in forgiveness for the sinner’s trespass.

questions.question: What continuous action concerning the fire on the altar is commanded in Leviticus 6:13?
options: The fire shall ever be burning and never go out
The fire is to be extinguished each morning
The fire is only lit during festival days
The fire must be replaced with incense
questions.correctAnswer: The fire shall ever be burning and never go out
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:13 commands the altar fire to always burn, symbolizing God's perpetual holiness and constant presence.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 6:15, what is done with a priest's handful of the meat offering?
options: It is burned on the altar as a sweet savour to the LORD
It is eaten by the entire congregation
It is given as a gift to the poor
It is buried outside the camp
questions.correctAnswer: It is burned on the altar as a sweet savour to the LORD
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:15 teaches that the priest burns the handful of the meat offering on the altar as a memorial and pleasing aroma to God.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 6:17 reveal about the sanctity of the meat offering given to Aaron and his sons?
options: It is most holy and must not be baked with leaven
It can be eaten anywhere at any time
It is common and may be shared with strangers
It is to be used only for animal feed
questions.correctAnswer: It is most holy and must not be baked with leaven
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:17 states the offering is most holy, like sin and trespass offerings, and must be unleavened, emphasizing purity and holiness.

questions.question: What is the perpetual nature of the meat offering commanded in Leviticus 6:20-22?
options: It is offered daily, half in the morning and half at night
It is offered once a year on the Day of Atonement
It is offered monthly during new moons
It is only offered during harvest festivals
questions.correctAnswer: It is offered daily, half in the morning and half at night
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:20-22 commands the continual, daily offering of the meat offering in two halves, symbolizing constant devotion and worship.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 6:25-27 describe the place and manner in which the sin offering is to be killed and its effect on holiness?
options: It is killed where the burnt offering is killed and makes all who touch it holy
It is killed outside the camp and is common
It is killed in the priests’ homes and must not be touched
It is killed by the offerer and burned completely
questions.correctAnswer: It is killed where the burnt offering is killed and makes all who touch it holy
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:25-27 shows the sin offering is killed at the same place as the burnt offering and that touching its flesh or blood conveys holiness.

questions.question: Which doctrinal truth is taught by the requirement in Leviticus 6:28 that the earthen vessel used to cook the sin offering be broken?
options: The impurity of sin’s consequences and the need for total removal
The permanency of sin’s forgiveness after cooking
The sanctity of household utensils for offerings
The allowance for reuse of vessels after washing
questions.correctAnswer: The impurity of sin’s consequences and the need for total removal
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:28 commands breaking the earthen vessel, symbolizing the irrevocable consequence of sin and the necessity of complete removal of impurity.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the detailed rituals in Leviticus 6:1-7 are merely legalistic and lack spiritual significance. What does this passage actually teach about sin and atonement?
options: It teaches that sin requires restitution and a spotless sacrifice for forgiveness
It teaches that verbal confession alone is sufficient
It teaches that sin can be ignored if one repents internally
It teaches that all sins are automatically forgiven without action
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that sin requires restitution and a spotless sacrifice for forgiveness
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:1-7 teaches that sin involves tangible wrongdoing requiring restitution plus a perfect ram offering for atonement, highlighting God's justice and mercy, countering claims of mere legalism.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching is conveyed by Leviticus 6:12-13 and Leviticus 6:23 about the altar fire and offerings?
options: The altar fire must never go out and all meat offerings for priests are wholly burnt
The altar fire is extinguished daily and offerings are shared with the people
The fire is symbolic and offerings can be eaten by anyone
The fire is to be replaced weekly and offerings are stored
questions.correctAnswer: The altar fire must never go out and all meat offerings for priests are wholly burnt
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:12-13 commands the perpetual fire on the altar, and 6:23 asserts that priestly meat offerings are wholly burnt, signifying God’s continuous holiness and total consecration of offerings.

questions.question: Leviticus 6:16-18 and 6:29 together reveal what about the sanctity and consumption of offerings by Aaron and his sons?
options: They may eat most offerings in a holy place, but only males and the offerings are most holy
They may eat all offerings anywhere, including women and children
Only the high priest may eat any part of the offerings
They are forbidden to eat any offerings for holiness reasons
questions.correctAnswer: They may eat most offerings in a holy place, but only males and the offerings are most holy
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:16-18 and 6:29 state that Aaron and his sons (males) eat the remainder of certain offerings in the holy place, emphasizing both the sanctity of offerings and the special priestly privilege.

questions.question: What theological insight about God's holiness and human sanctification is drawn from Leviticus 6:18 concerning those who touch the LORD’s offerings made by fire?
options: Everyone who touches them shall be holy
Only the high priest may touch the offerings
Touching offerings causes defilement
Offerings are common and may be handled casually
questions.correctAnswer: Everyone who touches them shall be holy
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:18 teaches that touching the LORD’s offerings makes a person holy, revealing God's attribute of holiness and the call for human sanctification through proximity to divine things.

questions.question: How do Leviticus 6:9-11 and 6:24-27 together illustrate the priestly duties related to the altar and sin offerings?
options: Priests maintain the altar fire, remove ashes properly, and eat the sin offering in the holy place
Priests only offer incense and do not touch the offerings
Priests delegate all duties to Levites and do not enter the tabernacle
Priests may eat sin offerings anywhere and extinguish the altar fire
questions.correctAnswer: Priests maintain the altar fire, remove ashes properly, and eat the sin offering in the holy place
questions.explanation: Leviticus 6:9-11 commands priests to maintain the altar fire and remove ashes properly; 6:24-27 mandates that priests eat sin offerings in the holy place, highlighting their sacred stewardship.
